data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

extract_result.subject: Telephone Use
extract_result.opi: Office of the Chief Information Officer, Digital Infrastructure Services Center, Enterprise Network Services
extract_result.purpose: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for the management and use of Government telephone equipment.
extract_result.scope: This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, contractors, data centers, cloud service providers, cooperative partners, and others working for, or on behalf of, the USDA.

actors.name: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
Managers responsible for telecommunications systems within Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
employees at customer service call centers, and at other locations where calls from the general public may be received
USDA customer service telephone numbers equipped with call monitoring or recording equipment
All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
components: Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors

actors.name: Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), Digital Infrastructure Services Center (DISC), Enterprise Network Services (ENS), Telecommunications Infrastructure Management and Governance (TIMG)
international, inter- and intra-Local Access and Transport Area (interLATA and intraLATA) telecommunications service providers

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for the management and use of Government telephone equipment.
policy_statements.target: management and use of Government telephone equipment

policy_statements.source_text: This DR replaces DR 3300-1-B, Telephone Use, dated March 23, 1999.
This DR will be in effect until superseded or the expiration date.
All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will align their policies and procedures with this DR within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices may supplement this DR when developing their internal guidance.
policy_statements.actor_name: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: when developing their internal guidance

policy_statements.source_text: Modifications to the intent or purpose of this DR are not allowed.
policy_statements.target: Modifications to the intent or purpose of this DR

policy_statements.source_text: If Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices publish internal guidance that supplements this DR, one copy of each supplement will be forwarded to the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), Digital Infrastructure Services Center (DISC), Enterprise Network Services (ENS), Telecommunications Infrastructure Management and Governance (TIMG) at ens.policy@ocio.usda.gov.
conditions: If Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices publish internal guidance that supplements this DR

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, contractors, data centers, cloud service providers, cooperative partners, and others working for, or on behalf of, the USDA.
policy_statements.target: all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, contractors, data centers, cloud service providers, cooperative partners, and others working for, or on behalf of, the USDA

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA telephone use policy depends on, and is derived from, the regulations promulgated by Congress and the Executive Office of the President.

Managers responsible for telecommunications systems within Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must be proactive in educating employees on telephone abuse to mitigate the risk of abuse and fraud to the systems.
policy_statements.actor_name: Managers responsible for telecommunications systems within Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: responsible for telecommunications systems within Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Telephone equipment that is paid by the Government is available for conducting official business or for limited personal use as outlined in this DR.
policy_statements.target: Telephone equipment that is paid by the Government
conditions: for conducting official business or for limited personal use as outlined in this DR

policy_statements.source_text: Official calls may include emergency calls and calls that Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices determine are necessary in the interest of the Government.
policy_statements.target: emergency calls and calls that Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices determine are necessary in the interest of the Government

policy_statements.source_text: Supervisors are responsible for the management of telephone use within the scope of their jurisdiction.
conditions: within the scope of their jurisdiction

policy_statements.source_text: Use of Government telephone equipment for limited personal use may be authorized if such use satisfies the following criteria:
policy_statements.target: Use of Government telephone equipment for limited personal use
conditions: if such use satisfies the following criteria

policy_statements.source_text: It is of reasonable duration and frequency;
It reasonably could not have been made at another time; and
It does not adversely affect the performance of the employee’s official duties.

Personal long distance toll and toll-free calls can be made during work hours using any type of Government telephone (e.g., cellular, smartphone, Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP), analog) if the call is consistent with the criteria specified in Section 5a(1).
policy_statements.target: Personal long distance toll and toll-free calls
conditions: during work hours
if the call is consistent with the criteria specified in Section 5a(1)

policy_statements.source_text: The following types of calls are prohibited when using Government equipment:
conditions: when using Government equipment

policy_statements.source_text: Calls that interfere with the performance of Government business; and
policy_statements.target: Calls that interfere with the performance of Government business

policy_statements.source_text: Calls to unsafe and unauthorized parties (e.g., “900” calls).
policy_statements.target: Calls to unsafe and unauthorized parties (e.g., “900” calls)

policy_statements.source_text: Incoming collect calls (calls placed from a non-Government number to a Federal Government number) and third-party calls are prohibited, except for official business and only when authorized in writing by the employee’s supervisor.
policy_statements.target: Incoming collect calls (calls placed from a non-Government number to a Federal Government number) and third-party calls
conditions: except for official business and only when authorized in writing by the employee’s supervisor

policy_statements.source_text: Since the telephone company charges an additional fee for collect calls, employees and their supervisors should consult with the Telecommunications Mission Area Control Officer (TMACO) to determine if there is an alternative, cost-effective method for accepting collect calls.
conditions: Since the telephone company charges an additional fee for collect calls

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will determine whether it is necessary to install Government-furnished telephones in an employee’s private residence.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: whether it is necessary to install Government-furnished telephones in an employee’s private residence

policy_statements.source_text: In general, this practice is discouraged to avoid possible conflicts of interest.
If it is acceptable for the employee to perform Government work on his or her personal telephone, the supervisor may allow telework without providing a Government-furnished telephone for offsite use.
conditions: If it is acceptable for the employee to perform Government work on his or her personal telephone

policy_statements.source_text: If it is mandated that an employee must use a Government telephone for telework, the employee must adhere to this policy.
conditions: If it is mandated that an employee must use a Government telephone for telework

policy_statements.source_text: In accordance with DR 1710-001, Interception and Monitoring of Telephone and Non-telephone Conversations, and DR 4070-735-001, Employee Responsibilities and Conduct, all parties on the call must receive prior and adequate notice that their call is being monitored and recorded, and all parties on the call must agree in advance to the monitoring and recording.
policy_statements.target: prior and adequate notice that their call is being monitored and recorded
cross_references: DR 1710-001, Interception and Monitoring of Telephone and Non-telephone Conversations

policy_statements.source_text: In accordance with DR 3300-001, Telecommunications & Internet Services and Use, and DR 1710-001, employees at customer service call centers, and at other locations where calls from the general public may be received, will be reminded that any such calls in which they participate may be monitored for evaluating the performance of employees and for quality control purposes.
policy_statements.actor_name: employees at customer service call centers, and at other locations where calls from the general public may be received
policy_statements.target: employees at customer service call centers, and at other locations where calls from the general public may be received
cross_references: DR 3300-001, Telecommunications & Internet Services and Use

policy_statements.source_text: USDA customer service telephone numbers equipped with call monitoring or recording equipment will provide a suitable greeting announcement such as: “This call may be recorded for quality control or training purposes.”
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA customer service telephone numbers equipped with call monitoring or recording equipment

policy_statements.source_text: Once the caller on the incoming call is connected to a live USDA employee, the caller should be given the opportunity to provide consent to the recording or monitoring of the call.
policy_statements.target: opportunity to provide consent to the recording or monitoring of the call
conditions: Once the caller on the incoming call is connected to a live USDA employee

policy_statements.source_text: The call cannot be recorded or monitored if the caller does not provide consent.
conditions: if the caller does not provide consent

policy_statements.source_text: For those calls that continue to be monitored or recorded, an automatic tone warning device, sometimes called a beep tone, will be provided.
conditions: For those calls that continue to be monitored or recorded

policy_statements.source_text: This tone would automatically produce a distinct signal that is repeated at regular intervals during the course of the telephone conversation when the recording or monitoring device is in use.
policy_statements.target: distinct signal that is repeated at regular intervals during the course of the telephone conversation
conditions: when the recording or monitoring device is in use

policy_statements.source_text: If speakerphones are used, all parties will be informed of the names of persons listening in prior to the subject matter of the call being introduced.
conditions: If speakerphones are used
prior to the subject matter of the call being introduced

policy_statements.source_text: The Office of Inspector General (OIG) has an exception to the requirement for consensual recording of conversations.
policy_statements.target: requirement for consensual recording of conversations

policy_statements.source_text: This exception is described in DR 1710-001, Section 3b(1).
Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will implement cost-effective actions to minimize their exposure to telephone abuse.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: cost-effective actions to minimize their exposure to telephone abuse

policy_statements.source_text: Abuse can be minimized by:
Reviewing and validating office telephone bills;
Blocking collect and third party calls through the Local Exchange Carrier (LEC) and telephone systems; and
Educating employees on the telephone use policy.
USDA personnel will report the loss of Government telephone equipment to their manager as soon as possible to enable services to be deactivated and tracked and to minimize financial losses.
conditions: as soon as possible

policy_statements.source_text: USDA personnel will comply with DR 3580-004, Securing Remote Access to USDA Information Systems and Client Devices and DR 3580-005, Securing Client Devices for International Travel, regarding the use of telephone equipment while traveling.
conditions: regarding the use of telephone equipment while traveling
cross_references: DR 3580-004, Securing Remote Access to USDA Information Systems and Client Devices
DR 3580-005, Securing Client Devices for International Travel

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) will:

Represent the USDA to the Federal CIO Council, General Services Administration (GSA), and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regarding requests for exceptions to mandatory telecommunications services contracts;
policy_statements.target: Federal CIO Council, General Services Administration (GSA), and Office of Management and Budget (OMB)
conditions: regarding requests for exceptions to mandatory telecommunications services contracts

policy_statements.source_text: Represent the USDA to oversight agencies, such as OMB, Government Accountability Office (GAO), Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Department of Commerce (DOC), and Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on telecommunications-related issues;
policy_statements.target: oversight agencies, such as OMB, Government Accountability Office (GAO), Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Department of Commerce (DOC), and Federal Communications Commission (FCC)

policy_statements.source_text: Respond to oversight agencies with timely and accurate USDA telecommunications program and cost information;
Serve as the USDA liaison with international, inter- and intra-Local Access and Transport Area (interLATA and intraLATA) telecommunications service providers;
policy_statements.target: international, inter- and intra-Local Access and Transport Area (interLATA and intraLATA) telecommunications service providers

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as the USDA representative to the Diplomatic Telecommunications Service Program Office (DTSPO); and
Perform management and oversight responsibilities in accordance with the Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), Public Law (P.L.) 113-291, as applicable to this directive.
conditions: as applicable to this directive
cross_references: Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), Public Law (P.L.) 113-291

policy_statements.source_text: The ENS Director will:
Establish procedures for monitoring, measuring, and enforcing compliance with this DR;
policy_statements.target: procedures for monitoring, measuring, and enforcing compliance with this DR

policy_statements.source_text: Oversee Mission Area, agency, and staff office compliance with USDA telecommunications policies and procedures;
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office compliance with USDA telecommunications policies and procedures

policy_statements.source_text: Manage USDA telecommunications services, equipment, and facilities in accordance with prescribed laws, regulations, standards, and related USDA 3300 Series telecommunications management directives;
policy_statements.target: USDA telecommunications services, equipment, and facilities

policy_statements.source_text: Review and render a decision for Mission Area, agency, and staff office policy waiver requests;
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office policy waiver requests

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain an electronic file of approved waivers;
Work with Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices to eliminate redundant or unused services and equipment;
policy_statements.target: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Include telecommunications requirements and initiatives as part of the telecommunications planning process;
Use GSA and USDA mandated programs when Mission Area, agency, and staff office requirements can be met cost-effectively through those programs;
conditions: when Mission Area, agency, and staff office requirements can be met cost-effectively through those programs

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain inventories of USDA telecommunications resources to the extent necessary to:
Ensure adequate and appropriate telecommunications resources to support the Mission Area, agency, and staff office mission;
Ensure accountability for USDA telecommunications property; and
Meet Departmental and Governmental requests for periodic or special inventory reports.
policy_statements.target: Departmental and Governmental requests for periodic or special inventory reports

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors will:
Ensure Mission Area, agency, and staff office personnel comply with this DR;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office personnel

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure Mission Area, agency, and staff office internal directives conform to this DR’s stated requirements;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office internal directives

policy_statements.source_text: Provide guidance, oversight, and training on the issuance and use of Government-furnished telecommunications in Government and non-Government buildings;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
policy_statements.target: guidance, oversight, and training on the issuance and use of Government-furnished telecommunications in Government and non-Government buildings

policy_statements.source_text: Include telecommunications requirements and initiatives as part of the telecommunications planning process;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Select the most cost-effective solution to meet the telephone needs of the office;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Implement cost-effective actions to minimize the exposure to telephone abuse;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
policy_statements.target: cost-effective actions to minimize the exposure to telephone abuse

policy_statements.source_text: Require supervisory personnel to authorize, in writing, the approval of all international calls that incur charges for USDA.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
conditions: that incur charges for USDA

policy_statements.source_text: Obtain waivers and approvals from the ENS Director when Mission Area, agency, and staff office telecommunications requirements cannot be met through mandated programs; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors
conditions: when Mission Area, agency, and staff office telecommunications requirements cannot be met through mandated programs

policy_statements.source_text: Provide the TMACO’s name and contact information to the DTSPO and USDA CIO.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office Information Technology (IT) Directors

policy_statements.source_text: The roles and responsibilities for TMACOs are provided in DR 3300-020, Telecommunications Mission Area Control Officer Roles and Responsibilities.
cross_references: DR 3300-020, Telecommunications Mission Area Control Officer Roles and Responsibilities

policy_statements.source_text: DR 4070-735-001, Section 16, sets forth USDA’s policies, procedures, and standards on employee responsibilities and conduct relative to the use of computers and telecommunications equipment.
DR 4070-735-001, Section 21, states that a violation of any of the responsibilities and conduct standards contained in this directive may be cause for disciplinary or adverse action; and

Such disciplinary or adverse action will be affected in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, including the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) regulations, OMB regulations, and the Standards of Ethical Conduct for Employees of the Executive Branch.
cross_references: Standards of Ethical Conduct for Employees of the Executive Branch

policy_statements.source_text: All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are required to conform to this policy.
policy_statements.actor_name: All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: If a specific policy requirement cannot be met as explicitly stated, Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices may submit a waiver request to the ENS Director for review and determination.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: If a specific policy requirement cannot be met as explicitly stated

policy_statements.source_text: Submit the waiver request to ens.policy@ocio.usda.gov.

The waiver request will explain the reason for the request, identify compensating controls and actions that meet the intent of the policy, and identify how the compensating controls and actions provide a similar or greater level of defense or compliance than the policy requirement.

The USDA telephone use policy depends on, and is derived from, the regulations promulgated by Congress and the Executive Office of the President.

Managers responsible for telecommunications systems within Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must be proactive in educating employees on telephone abuse to mitigate the risk of abuse and fraud to the systems.
Managers responsible for telecommunications systems within Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
responsible for telecommunications systems within Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
Telephone equipment that is paid by the Government is available for conducting official business or for limited personal use as outlined in this DR.
Telephone equipment that is paid by the Government
for conducting official business or for limited personal use as outlined in this DR
Official calls may include emergency calls and calls that Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices determine are necessary in the interest of the Government.
emergency calls and calls that Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices determine are necessary in the interest of the Government
Supervisors are responsible for the management of telephone use within the scope of their jurisdiction.
within the scope of their jurisdiction
Use of Government telephone equipment for limited personal use may be authorized if such use satisfies the following criteria:
Use of Government telephone equipment for limited personal use
if such use satisfies the following criteria
It is of reasonable duration and frequency;
It reasonably could not have been made at another time; and
It does not adversely affect the performance of the employee’s official duties.

Personal long distance toll and toll-free calls can be made during work hours using any type of Government telephone (e.g., cellular, smartphone, Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP), analog) if the call is consistent with the criteria specified in Section 5a(1).
Personal long distance toll and toll-free calls
if the call is consistent with the criteria specified in Section 5a(1)
The following types of calls are prohibited when using Government equipment:
Calls that interfere with the performance of Government business; and
Calls that interfere with the performance of Government business
Calls to unsafe and unauthorized parties (e.g., “900” calls).
Calls to unsafe and unauthorized parties (e.g., “900” calls)

Incoming collect calls (calls placed from a non-Government number to a Federal Government number) and third-party calls are prohibited, except for official business and only when authorized in writing by the employee’s supervisor.
Incoming collect calls (calls placed from a non-Government number to a Federal Government number) and third-party calls
except for official business and only when authorized in writing by the employee’s supervisor

Since the telephone company charges an additional fee for collect calls, employees and their supervisors should consult with the Telecommunications Mission Area Control Officer (TMACO) to determine if there is an alternative, cost-effective method for accepting collect calls.
Since the telephone company charges an additional fee for collect calls
Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will determine whether it is necessary to install Government-furnished telephones in an employee’s private residence.
Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
whether it is necessary to install Government-furnished telephones in an employee’s private residence
In general, this practice is discouraged to avoid possible conflicts of interest.
If it is acceptable for the employee to perform Government work on his or her personal telephone, the supervisor may allow telework without providing a Government-furnished telephone for offsite use.

USDA customer service telephone numbers equipped with call monitoring or recording equipment will provide a suitable greeting announcement such as: “This call may be recorded for quality control or training purposes.”
USDA customer service telephone numbers equipped with call monitoring or recording equipment
Once the caller on the incoming call is connected to a live USDA employee, the caller should be given the opportunity to provide consent to the recording or monitoring of the call.
opportunity to provide consent to the recording or monitoring of the call
Once the caller on the incoming call is connected to a live USDA employee
The call cannot be recorded or monitored if the caller does not provide consent.
if the caller does not provide consent
For those calls that continue to be monitored or recorded, an automatic tone warning device, sometimes called a beep tone, will be provided.
For those calls that continue to be monitored or recorded
This tone would automatically produce a distinct signal that is repeated at regular intervals during the course of the telephone conversation when the recording or monitoring device is in use.
distinct signal that is repeated at regular intervals during the course of the telephone conversation
when the recording or monitoring device is in use
If speakerphones are used, all parties will be informed of the names of persons listening in prior to the subject matter of the call being introduced.
prior to the subject matter of the call being introduced
The Office of Inspector General (OIG) has an exception to the requirement for consensual recording of conversations.
requirement for consensual recording of conversations
This exception is described in DR 1710-001, Section 3b(1).

USDA personnel will report the loss of Government telephone equipment to their manager as soon as possible to enable services to be deactivated and tracked and to minimize financial losses.
